olivia_customer: Hey team — we're hitting consistent JSON parse failures when using structured_output=true with streaming enabled. Client side JSONDecodeError after concatenating chunks. Repro below, attaching raw chunk capture.

olivia_customer: Raw HTTP chunk capture (we pasted the exact bytes):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

19
{"response":"This is a multiline string with a trailing backslash \

1a
and it continues","meta":{"note":"contains unicode — dash"}}
0

```

olivia_customer: If you concat the chunks you get an invalid string because the backslash at the end of chunk 1 escapes the newline/quote boundary. The python client fails with: `JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 23 (char 22)`.

maria_support: Thanks — sorry about that. Can you confirm: 1) model name, 2) SDK+version, 3) are you using streaming=true (you said yes) and which endpoint (/generate?), 4) request-id or trace-id from response headers? Also would be super helpful to get the exact prompt (any literal backslashes) and whether the input contains Windows CRLFs.

olivia_customer: Model: redwood-13b-stream-v2, SDK: python-client v0.10.1, endpoint: POST /v1/generate, streaming=true. Request-ID header from one example: rwd-3f2b9c. Prompt contains a small markdown block with a Windows path (C:\Users\dev\notes.md) and some pasted text with newlines. Repro steps we used:
1) call generate with structured_output=true and streaming=true
2) capture raw chunks from our proxy (we saved the exact bytes above)
3) concatenate chunks and attempt json.loads() -> fails
4) repeat with streaming=false -> works fine (full JSON returned).

jamal_eng: :eyes: thanks for the clear repro. This looks like a streaming chunk boundary bug where the encoder is leaving a trailing backslash at the end of a chunk when escaping backslashes/quotes. If a chunk ends with `\` or `"` and the decoder naively concatenates, you can end up with a half-escaped sequence. Two quick asks: can you 1) paste any shortened prompt that reproduces this (we only need a tiny example), and 2) does the problem still reproduce if you normalize CRLF -> LF on the client before sending?

olivia_customer: Short prompt that reproduces: `Please format the following path as JSON: C:\\temp\\log.txt
Also include a dash — in the reason.` Normalizing CRLF to LF on client reduced frequency but didn't eliminate it. Streaming off is reliable.

kevin_sre: Ticket-bot, create internal issue for eng-runtime: streaming encoder leaving half-escaped bytes at chunk boundaries, reproducer attached. Priority: high for customer impact. @jamal_eng can you take?

ticket-bot: Created issue RWD-STREAM-4485 and linked request-id rwd-3f2b9c.

jamal_eng: I'll take it. Immediate workaround for customers: 1) disable streaming (streaming=false) or 2) set structured_output=false and parse server text body with a tolerant JSON sanitizer on client. Longer term fix: avoid splitting in the middle of escape sequences or ensure the receiver buffers until escapes are closed. I have a local repro and suspect the change landed in commit 9f4c2ae (encoder:escape-handling).

maria_support: I'll offer credits and keep the customer updated. Olivia, sorry for the disruption — we'll aim to patch the runtime and cut a hotfix tomorrow. Can you confirm if you want us to proactively patch your Dedicated instance (if applicable) or just notify when hosted rollout is scheduled?

olivia_customer: Hosted only, please notify. Disabling streaming is OK as a temporary fix for us. Thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:

jamal_eng: Plan: 1) triage and confirm repro on staging, 2) create hotfix branch to avoid split-escape across chunk boundaries, 3) run integration tests with inputs containing backslashes and CRLFs, 4) roll out to hosted and notify. I'll update RWD-STREAM-4485 with ETA.

kevin_sre: Also adding monitoring rule to catch an uptick in JSONDecodeError counts for /v1/generate.

maria_support: Noted — we'll follow up in the ticket thread and keep you posted.

olivia_customer: Thanks everyone, appreciate the fast responses.
